newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CSR looks to price increases.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CSR looks to price increases.

text.p: Building materials and aluminium group CSR Ltd said on Monday it would focus on price increases rather than market share in the forseeable future and that it believed the profitable U.S. operations would continue to grow.
Managing director Geoff Kells told an analysts briefing after the release of the first half results that the company was not going to wait for the depressed Australian housing market to improve.
Kells said the company had taken the view that price increases were more important than market share because it would benefit shareholders in the longer term.
It had also adopted a policy of active asset management, which involved focusing on high growth areas outside Australia such as the United States and Asia.
Kells said CSR America was expected to continue growing.
"There is a fairly bullish result in America and as far as we can see, while the market for us is a bit toppy, we don't as yet see any fall-off," he said.
Kells said CSR also expected more asset sales in the second half of 1996/97, with 35 building and construction plants and 17 plants in the United States.
He said CSR had raised A$139 million from asset sales since the divestment programme was announced earlier this year.
Kells said the sugar market remained difficult, with the company estimating the raw sugar price at about A$340 a tonne this year compared with A$380 a tonne last year.
He said the refined sugar market remained very competitive, with a price war amongst producers continuing and lower prices likely to continue into calendar 1997.
He said the aluminium sector remained weak, with world prices 17 percent lower than a year ago.
The company would have a lower level of hedging in the second half and a decision would soon be on whether to increase capacity at the Tomago smelter north of Sydney.
